clue.text: Making a point, lie or make some distortion

parts.note: W is west, a point of the compass
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone making an argument twists the truth with a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point here, not an argument's point.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest words is to twist their meaning, a deliberate distortion.

clue.text: Dicky came in to see the pictures

indicators.note: dicky is slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters of the following words are put out of order

explanation.surface: A man with a dodgy heart walks in to catch a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British slang for unsound or weak; it rearranges CAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage 'the pictures' means a film theatre, the place where movies are shown.

definitions.meaning: staff who help actors into their costumes backstage
sideboards with shelves for plates and crockery

explanation.surface: The kitchen gear belonging to the backstage crew of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre costume helpers share a name with the shelved sideboards that hold crockery in a kitchen.

clue.text: Kept taking one in, as is well, remembered

indicators.note: taking with 'in' says one piece is drawn into the middle of another
together with 'taking', this signals that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: goods kept away are stored
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone kept taking a lodger in, as people well remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking ... in' is split by 'one': the I goes inside STORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something storied is celebrated in tales and legend, so long remembered by many.

indicators.note: a problem here suggests the letters are in a muddle and must be worked out

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plain plural, giving its letter S

explanation.surface: Whether a man is a sinner or a saint is the real question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint's' keeps its S as a letter; OR plus SAINTS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser commits a serious wrongdoing, so counts as an offender or sinner.

clue.text: Driving around in reverse can be very taxing

indicators.note: around says the first piece wraps about the second one

parts.note: driving forward is pushing

indicators.note: reverse turns the little word in backwards, so it reads the other way

explanation.surface: Driving with the car in reverse can be hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In reverse' reads like a gear; only 'reverse' is the signal, turning the little word 'in', and 'around' puts the result inside the synonym for driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishing schedule or climb is gruelling, extremely demanding.

parts.note: a little is a bit
to rate someone is an old word for to scold them

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling someone a proper little nag.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold or berate is an old sense still used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee would.

indicators.note: catching here says the first piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in that sense
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A lawyer landing a fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer; it is one who solicits business, a TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game species of the salmon family, prized by anglers.

clue.text: A cold man will cause suffering

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A chilly fellow is going to bring hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is a form of physical suffering.

clue.text: The fool mistreating roses he values

parts.note: a fool is an ass

indicators.note: mistreating the flowers knocks their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy gardener damaging roses he cherishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Values' looks like a noun after 'he'; it is a verb, so 'he values' is a person who appraises.
explanation.definitionFit: One who values property or damage for tax or insurance purposes is a valuer.

parts.note: to cut is to chop
something popular is in

explanation.surface: Someone trims a hit from a pop musician's set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular music' reads as a phrase, but 'music man' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish Romantic composer of piano works, a celebrated musician.

clue.text: In South Africa few dine in a restaurant

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In South Africa only a few people eat out at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small eating place serving light meals and coffee.

clue.text: People rowing about acquiescence can make sense

indicators.note: about here means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight
acquiescence is saying yes

explanation.surface: Rowers quarrelling over agreement could see reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' looks like quarrelling; it is oarsmen, a crew of EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five human senses.

parts.note: a painting fit for the tiny people of Gulliver's Travels: a very small portrait

explanation.surface: A painting made by the tiny folk of Lilliput.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilliput is the land of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels; 'Lilliputian' means tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small detailed portrait painting suits the tiny-scale people of Lilliput.

indicators.note: works is read as a verb, the letters being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Revised works covering all sorts of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun, books revised; it is the verb rearranging REVISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means varied, of many different sorts.

definitions.meaning: the act of passing inside, or a doorway
to captivate or delight, as a verb with stress on the second syllable

explanation.surface: Joining for the sake of its appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a way in or the act of coming in; the verb means to captivate or bewitch.

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to guard is to tend, as one tends a flock

explanation.surface: An argument against having guards.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend a claim is to argue against it or challenge it.

indicators.note: characters here are the letters of the two words, to be arranged anew

explanation.surface: A severe sullen fellow refusing to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people; it means letters, those of BEAT DOUR, reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An obdurate person refuses to change their mind, hard-hearted and unyielding.

clue.text: Senior students-only half managed to turn up

parts.note: semi is the prefix meaning half

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Only half the senior students bothered to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like attending; in this down clue it reverses RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small university class for advanced students discussing a topic with a tutor.

clue.text: Assist retired folk and there's strong criticism

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to assist is to aid
a folk or people is a tribe

explanation.surface: Helping pensioners, and it brings harsh complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like pensioners; it reverses AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter verbal attack or tirade against someone.

clue.text: Hostelries in the capitals of Norway and Sweden

indicators.note: the capitals are the capital letters at the start of each country name

explanation.surface: Pubs found in the capital cities of Norway and Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests Oslo and Stockholm; it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelries are places offering lodging and drink, like old roadside taverns.

definitions.meaning: timber from fir or pine trees

explanation.surface: Longing for an accord.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names softwood timber such as fir or pine, and also a bargain struck between parties.

definitions.meaning: a month of summer in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: Summer's a wonderful season!
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month falls in summer; as an adjective, with stress on the second syllable, it means majestic or venerable.

definitions.meaning: the hard seed of a cherry or plum

explanation.surface: A rocky quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a piece of rock, and the hard kernel of a plum is also called by the same name.

definitions.meaning: a line of descent, breed or lineage
to exert or stretch to the limit

explanation.surface: The household under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed or lineage is one sense; to exert great effort or stretch is the other.

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: incensed means very angry, irate
to deck out or rig out is to dress up

explanation.surface: Furious because the ship's deck is soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship; it is the verb to dress up, RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water.

clue.text: The builder a guy one may rely on

definitions.meaning: the block a builder lays in a wall

definitions.text: a guy one may rely on
definitions.meaning: a dependable, good-hearted person, in old slang

explanation.surface: The builder is a dependable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a brick' is old British slang for a staunch, helpful friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay block used in building, and in slang a reliable stalwart friend.

clue.text: Supporters will be provided with parking by working men

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
artisans are skilled working men

explanation.surface: Workers who back a cause will get parking spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans are committed adherents of a cause or party.
